language.script_notes: Ukrainian Cyrillic with і, ї, є and ґ; the west is the most exclusively Ukrainian-speaking part of the country, and minority languages such as Hungarian and Romanian appear in Transcarpathia near the borders.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national; more common on winding Carpathian mountain roads.
road_furniture.curb_style: Cobblestone streets and tram lines in Lviv's historic center.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national, including white-painted pole bases and flag-coloured roadside objects.

architecture.roof_style: Multi-tiered shingled roofs with small domes on Carpathian wooden churches; steep tiled roofs on Habsburg-era buildings.
architecture.roof_material: Wooden shingle on churches and traditional houses; clay tile and metal on newer buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Timber-log churches in Hutsul, Boyko and Lemko styles (eight are UNESCO-listed); dense Habsburg-era masonry facades in Lviv with Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque influences; Central European-style plastered houses.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Weathered dark wood on churches; cream, ochre and pastel plaster on historic town buildings.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Carpathian wooden churches (Ukraine has over 2,500 across the country, with the highest concentration in the west); Lviv's cobbled Old Town, Baroque churches and trams; Transcarpathian Reformed churches and Hungarian-influenced architecture.

nature.vegetation: Dense spruce and beech forest and mountain meadows in the Carpathians; hay meadows and orchards in the foothills.
nature.terrain: The Carpathian Mountains — the only true mountain range in mainland Ukraine, with peaks over 2,000m such as Hoverla — rise above rolling foothills.
nature.climate_signature: Cooler and wetter than the rest of Ukraine, with snow-capped ridges in winter and a distinctly Central European feel.

vehicles.plate_color: As national — region letters such as 'BC' for Lviv Oblast.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Used Central and Western European imports (especially German and Czech brands) are more visible here than older Ladas; trams operate in Lviv.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage of Lviv and the main highways, dating mostly from around 2015; thinner in remote Carpathian valleys.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared border region, Habsburg and Central European architecture, wooden church traditions on both sides of the Carpathians
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Cyrillic versus Latin script; Poland's red-striped one-sided bollard and red-outlined yellow warning triangles are absent in Ukraine.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Carpathian terrain and mountain villages across the borders
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Ukrainian Cyrillic signage and Ukrainian blue-and-yellow plate strips separate the country; Slovakia's white-on-black house numbers and Romania's holey poles are absent.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The west has Carpathian mountains, wooden churches and Habsburg-era towns; the center and east are flat black-earth farmland and steppe with Soviet blocks and whitewashed mazanka houses.
